dissents.topic: Severity of `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` idiom in Basic Usage

positions.position: P1 — obscures intent, not idiomatic; prefer `pipeline.nodes[0]` or filter by name
P1 — gratuitous cleverness; `pipeline.nodes[0]` is shorter and obvious; example likely never executed
P1 — relies on undocumented iteration order; pretends a single-node pipeline is general; UNREASONED
P2 — cleverness without payoff, but a small teaching nit, not a blocker

dissents.topic: Severity of the `meta` field doing two jobs (user metadata vs. renderer config)

positions.position: P1 — leaky abstraction; collisions are undefined; needs separate fields or reserved namespace
P2 — complected concerns admitted in docs; should at least namespace or split
P2 — smell worth naming, but doc-level flag is sufficient; not a blocker

dissents.topic: Whether the Preview API design itself is appropriate (separate from doc quality)

positions.position: The underlying design — small tagged payload types with content + meta — is the right primitive; data dominates; no structural objection
EASY-NOT-SIMPLE — seven near-identical classes where one tagged value would do; node identity complected with presentation-time callable; CustomPreview escape hatch reveals the taxonomy is wrong
SPEC-MISSING — the supertype contract, substitutability, error semantics, and module boundary (kedro vs kedro-viz) are not stated; experimental warning is not a substitute for the spec

dissents.topic: Whether to split the PR (Vale config edits vs docs)

positions.position: P1 — THREE-PATCHES; Vale headings, Vale ignore, and the docs are independent changes and should be separate commits at minimum
P2 — minor hygiene; a one-line note explaining the lowercase `polars` addition would suffice
P2 — unreasoned duplication of `polars`/`Polars`; explain the precondition or fix Vale's case sensitivity

dissents.topic: Severity of the `preview_fn` lifecycle / contract being undocumented

positions.position: P1 — preconditions, postconditions, invariants, error semantics, and return-type contract of node.preview() are all absent; this is precisely what ADT discipline prevents
P1 — lifecycle of `node.preview()` is never specified (when called, by whom, at what cost); reader cannot reason about side effects or caching
P1 — preview complects identity, value, and time; best-practices list is etiquette compensating for missing contract on purity, cost, failure
P2 — doc should clarify, but the underlying data shape is fine; flagging via best-practice item 5 alone is hand-wavy
P2 — best-practice item 5 is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE; needs concrete precondition/postcondition reasoning, not vague try/except advice

issues.description: Basic-usage example uses `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` — obscure, non-idiomatic, and relies on undocumented iteration order
issues.detail: The line `training_node = next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` is equivalent to `pipeline.nodes[0]` but harder to read, likely never executed in a REPL, and only correct because the pipeline has exactly one node. A reader copying this pattern into a multi-node pipeline will silently retrieve some other node. Prefer `pipeline.nodes[0]` or filter by name: `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes if n.name == 'train_model_node')`.

issues.description: Multiple `node(...)` snippets appear as bare top-level expressions outside any `Pipeline([...])`, not runnable as shown
issues.detail: In the Mermaid customisation, Text-with-syntax-highlighting, and closure examples, `node(func=..., preview_fn=..., name=...)` is shown as a free-floating statement with no surrounding pipeline and no assignment. A reader copy-pasting will hit NameError or a dangling expression that has no effect. Either wrap each in a `Pipeline([...])` literal like the first example or annotate clearly that these are fragments.

issues.description: `preview_from_dataframe` / `preview_from_polars` examples take a DataFrame argument, contradicting the stated contract that preview_fn receives no inputs
issues.detail: The Table preview section shows `def preview_from_dataframe(df: pd.DataFrame) -> TablePreview` and `def preview_from_polars(df) -> TablePreview` as if they could be passed to `preview_fn=`. But the docs themselves state 100 lines later that 'Preview functions don't have access to node inputs or outputs directly'. `preview_fn` is invoked with no arguments by `node.preview()`. Either rewrite as zero-arg closures matching the later closure pattern, or label them explicitly as helpers to be wrapped.

issues.description: Lifecycle, return-type, and error contract of `preview_fn` / `node.preview()` are never specified
issues.detail: The docs never answer: Is `preview_fn` called eagerly at pipeline construction, lazily on `.preview()`, or only by Kedro-Viz? Is it called once per run or on every viz refresh? Same process? Does node.preview() return None when preview_fn is unset? Does it cache? What happens if preview_fn raises — propagate, swallow, wrap? Without these invariants the reader cannot reason about side effects, caching, or 'access datasets within the preview function'. The best-practices list compensates for this with etiquette rather than a contract.

issues.description: Preview supertype contract and substitutability requirements are never stated
issues.detail: JsonPreview, TablePreview, PlotlyPreview, MermaidPreview, ImagePreview, TextPreview, CustomPreview are presented as siblings of an implied supertype. The docs never state: every subtype guarantees `to_dict()` returns a serializable mapping with a known discriminator; content schemas are no weaker than the supertype's promise; meta is treated uniformly. TablePreview narrows content to list[dict], which is only sound if the supertype never promised arbitrary content. State the supertype contract, then prove each subtype substitutes.

issues.description: `meta` is overloaded with two distinct responsibilities (user metadata vs renderer configuration) — leaky abstraction
issues.detail: The 'Adding metadata to previews' section explicitly says meta serves two purposes: general user metadata and rendering configuration consumed by Kedro-Viz (Mermaid config, `language` for syntax highlighting). These are different contracts with different consumers. A user who puts `{'language': 'python'}` as metadata on a TextPreview accidentally triggers renderer behavior; key collisions with user metadata are undefined. The right design is two fields (e.g., `meta` for user data, `render_config` for renderer hints) or a reserved namespace. At minimum, document reserved keys per subtype and precedence rules.

issues.description: Mermaid `custom_config` mixes Mermaid-native keys with Kedro-Viz-specific `textStyle` without flagging the distinction
issues.detail: The example puts `securityLevel`, `flowchart`, and `themeVariables` (real Mermaid config keys) next to `textStyle` (described as 'CSS styling for text nodes'). The footnote links the Mermaid schema for 'a complete list of available Mermaid configuration options', implying all keys are Mermaid keys — but `textStyle` is not in the Mermaid schema. This leaks Kedro-Viz frontend CSS concerns into what is documented as Mermaid pass-through config, couples the public contract to a specific renderer, and leaves unknown-key behavior undefined.

issues.description: Module boundary unclear: kedro core docs are documenting kedro-viz rendering behavior
issues.detail: `kedro.pipeline.preview_contract` sits in kedro core, but the contract being described is dominated by what Kedro-Viz does with the payload (renderer_key, language highlighting, Mermaid config merging with 'sensible defaults'). Kedro core should own only the data shape and serialization contract; rendering policy belongs in kedro-viz docs and code. As written, the kedro contract will change every time the viz frontend changes. Draw the line: kedro promises the payload shape; kedro-viz documents how it renders it.

issues.description: CustomPreview `renderer_key` has no contract for registration, namespace, collision, or unknown-key handling
issues.detail: CustomPreview is the explicit extension point but the docs say only that renderer_key 'identifies which frontend component should handle rendering this preview'. The contract must answer: who owns the key namespace; how is collision with built-in renderers (json, table, plotly, mermaid, image, text) avoided; what does a consumer do for an unknown key (ignore, fallback, error); is content validated by kedro or opaque pass-through. Without these answers CustomPreview is an open-ended escape hatch that will fragment across users and break forward compatibility.

issues.description: Closure pattern for 'data context' silently teaches a build-time/run-time confusion
issues.detail: The 'Use closure to capture context' example bakes a hardcoded sample_data list into preview_fn at pipeline-construction time. The captured value is pinned for the life of the node, but the node runs later against different data. The doc presents this as the solution for 'preview based on actual data' without naming the time mismatch — the preview will lie about the run. Either show the real pattern (load the dataset by name from the catalog inside preview_fn) or state explicitly that preview_fn is decoupled from node I/O and closures only help with static context.

issues.description: Section promises dataset access in preview_fn but never shows how
issues.detail: The 'Using preview functions with data context' section states preview functions 'can use closures or access datasets within the preview function' — but only the closure pattern is demonstrated. If dataset access is supported and recommended, show it with the catalog handle and lifecycle warnings. If it's not really supported, drop the claim. Half-promises in docs become support tickets.

issues.description: Preview API complects node identity with a presentation-time callable
issues.detail: A node is an identity (a named step in a pipeline). A preview is a value at some time. Stapling preview_fn onto the node complects the structural identity of the pipeline step with a presentation-time callable unrelated to the computation. The docs should at minimum name that the preview is a value computed at a different time than the node executes, and that node.preview() is a separate temporal event from node.run() — otherwise users will reach for closures to smuggle data across that time boundary.

issues.description: Seven near-identical Preview classes where one tagged value would do
issues.detail: JsonPreview, TablePreview, PlotlyPreview, MermaidPreview, ImagePreview, TextPreview, CustomPreview all wrap a content field and optional meta. The kind is itself a value (a tag), and dispatch belongs at the renderer. A single Preview value with explicit :kind would serialise more naturally (to_dict() already flattens it) and would not need a CustomPreview escape hatch — every preview would already be 'custom' by virtue of its renderer_key. The docs at minimum should acknowledge these are tags over the same shape.

issues.description: Three logically independent patches landed in one PR (Vale headings, Vale ignore, docs)
issues.detail: The diff touches `.github/styles/Kedro/headings.yml` (add JSON exception), `.github/styles/Kedro/ignore.txt` (add lowercase polars), and `docs/build/nodes.md` (feature docs). These are three independent changes. The Vale tweaks are byproducts of getting docs to lint and should be their own commit so a future bisect or revert of the docs change doesn't drag along orthogonal style-config edits.

issues.description: Lowercase `polars` added to ignore.txt alongside existing `Polars` — papering over a spelling issue
issues.detail: `Polars` is already on the ignore list. Adding lowercase `polars` means the prose somewhere writes the brand name lowercased (likely `df.head(5).to_dicts()` style). Either fix the prose (Polars is a proper noun), explain the precondition in a comment/commit, or fix Vale's case sensitivity once rather than per-word. As written the addition is unexplained duplication.

issues.description: PR checklist admits no tests for the feature; docs assert API contracts not anchored to any test
issues.detail: The PR checklist shows tests and RELEASE.md unchecked. Defensible for a docs-only PR — but the docs assert concrete API contracts (`preview_fn` kwarg, `node.preview()` method, `to_dict()` on every preview type, `meta` keys like `language`, Mermaid config schema, CustomPreview.renderer_key) that aren't covered by tests in this diff. If #5317 reshapes the API, these docs silently lie. Recommend a doctest harness over the basic-usage block and citations to the source module.

issues.description: `ImagePreview` example contains unreachable / dead code after an unconditional `return`
issues.detail: The function ends with `return ImagePreview(content='https://...')` followed by a commented-out `return ImagePreview(content='data:image/png;base64,...')`. The structure suggests a function can do both. Split into two named functions (Option 1 / Option 2, as the Table preview section does) or use a single function with a clear `if/else`. Pedagogy-wise, dead code in examples is misleading.

issues.description: ImagePreview accepts URL or data URI in the same `content` field with no discriminator
issues.detail: ImagePreview.content can be either an external URL or an inline base64 data URI, distinguished only by string prefix. A URL is an identity pointing to something that may change; a data URI is a value frozen at preview time. Consumers must sniff the prefix to render correctly. Either add a `kind` field (url | data_uri) or document the prefix-sniffing rule as the contract so every renderer behaves identically; also flag the trust/caching/time differences.

issues.description: MermaidPreview content is an opaque DSL string with embedded styling — escapes the type system
issues.detail: MermaidPreview.content is a triple-quoted Mermaid DSL string including `style A fill:#e1f5ff` directives mixed in with graph topology. Two concerns (structure vs visual styling) are complected inside an opaque blob the preview type cannot inspect or validate. The docs should be honest that MermaidPreview is essentially a TextPreview with a renderer hint, otherwise users will expect validation/transformation that won't happen.

issues.description: Mermaid `custom_config` annotates upstream Mermaid defaults inline — will drift
issues.detail: The custom_config block annotates each key with `(default: 250)`, `(default: 50)`, etc. Those defaults belong to upstream Mermaid, not Kedro. The moment Mermaid changes a default, this doc is silently wrong. Either drop the `(default: X)` annotations and link to the schema (which is already linked), or generate them from upstream. Hand-maintained mirrors of upstream defaults are a maintenance trap.

issues.description: Mermaid config example shows every knob at once — too clever for an intro doc
issues.detail: The generate_mermaid_preview example pulls in securityLevel, nodeSpacing, rankSpacing, curve, themeVariables, and a textStyle block before the reader has a working preview. This is framework-shaped documentation: every knob shown at once. Prefer one minimal Mermaid example, then a short 'advanced: meta accepts a Mermaid config' subsection with a link.

issues.description: TextPreview `meta.language` accepted values and fallback are under-documented
issues.detail: The doc says 'Kedro-Viz supports `python`, `javascript`, and `yaml` highlighting.' What happens for unsupported values — silent fallback to plain text, error, raw output? A reader writing `meta={'language': 'sql'}` deserves to know. One short sentence on the fallback behaviour closes the gap.

issues.description: `preview.to_dict()` is computed and discarded in Basic Usage — unused variable / incidental object
issues.detail: The Basic Usage block computes `preview_dict = preview.to_dict()` and then does nothing with it. If the consumer always needs the dict, the rich object is incidental complexity between the function and the wire format. Either drop the line, show what it's for ('send to a frontend / write to JSON'), or rethink whether preview() should just return data. As written, the first thing the reader is shown to do with the returned value is unwrap it.

issues.description: Best-practice item 5 ('Handle errors: wrap preview logic in try-except if needed') is vague / defensive-as-substitute
issues.detail: Recommending try/except as a general best practice without stating what the precondition is, what exceptions are anticipated, or what to return on failure trains readers to swallow errors rather than reason about them. The doc should specify the contract — preview_fn exceptions are caught and surfaced as X, or wrapped as ErrorPreview, or propagated — and drop the bullet otherwise. Best-practice items that depend on 'if needed' are not best practices.

issues.description: Best Practices reads like etiquette compensating for a missing contract
issues.detail: 'Keep previews lightweight', 'make previews fast', 'avoid expensive computations', 'handle errors', 'test preview functions' — each is a workaround for the fact that preview_fn is an arbitrary callable invoked at an undefined time by an undefined caller, with no contract about cost, purity, or failure. The right answer is a clearer contract ('preview functions must be pure, must not perform I/O without an explicit dataset accessor, may raise PreviewError'), not bulleted etiquette.

issues.description: Experimental warning is quiet about which surfaces are likely to change
issues.detail: The warning correctly flags the feature as experimental, but the docs then teach seven concrete import paths, a closure pattern, and a renderer_key convention as if settled. The experimental notice should call out which surfaces are most likely to change (the seven-class taxonomy, meta overloading, renderer_key contract) so users can make informed coupling decisions.

issues.description: Experimental warning uses a relative link to `../about/experimental.md` — fragile
issues.detail: Relative links inside MkDocs admonitions are fragile across navigation depths and section moves; if `docs/about/experimental.md` is later relocated or rendered under a different URL, the link rots silently. The bracketed display text also shows the absolute repo path while the target is relative. Verify the link resolves in the rendered site and prefer a canonical docs URL or MkDocs cross-reference.

issues.description: Best-practice 'test preview functions' lacks an actionable example
issues.detail: The bullet tells readers to test preview functions but doesn't show how. A 6-line example using `assert isinstance(node.preview(), JsonPreview)` would make the best practice actionable. If you tell the reader to test, show them the shape.

issues.description: PR omits a RELEASE.md entry for a new user-facing feature surface
issues.detail: Two checklist items are unchecked: RELEASE.md and tests. Documenting a new public surface (`preview_fn` kwarg, `preview_contract` module, `node.preview()`) without a RELEASE.md note means downstream users won't be told the feature exists. Add a one-line entry under the appropriate experimental-features section pointing at the new docs page.

issues.description: Docs assert behaviour of `preview_contract` types and `node.preview()` without a single executable verification
issues.detail: Every snippet here is TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best — in fact not even tested, merely written. The docs assert that `preview.to_dict()` exists on every preview type, that CustomPreview takes `renderer_key`, that `meta` accepts `language` for TextPreview, that MermaidPreview merges its config with Kedro-Viz defaults. None of these claims are anchored to a doctest or a linked test, so the documentation will drift the moment the implementation moves. At minimum, a doctest harness over basic-usage and citations to the source module.

issues.description: Underlying preview API data shape is sound — data dominates
issues.detail: Despite the documentation issues, the underlying design — small tagged payload types (Json/Table/Plotly/Mermaid/Image/Text/Custom) with content + optional meta — is the right primitive. The rendering algorithm follows from the data tag. SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE applies to the API being documented. Noted as a counterweight to the structural critiques: no structural objection to the data shape itself.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges that this is a docs-only PR for an experimental `preview_fn` feature with clear prose and good per-preview-type coverage, but with significant rigor gaps in the examples and the underlying contract. Strongest shared claims: (1) the Basic Usage `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` idiom is non-idiomatic and likely unexecuted (flagged by four reviewers); (2) several `node(...)` snippets are bare expressions outside any Pipeline and not runnable as shown (three reviewers); (3) the `meta` field is openly overloaded as both user metadata and renderer configuration, a leaky abstraction the docs admit but don't resolve (three reviewers); (4) the closure pattern for 'data context' teaches a build-time/run-time confusion that will produce previews that lie about runs (four reviewers); (5) the lifecycle, error semantics, and return contract of `preview_fn` / `node.preview()` are never specified, leaving best-practices etiquette in place of a contract (three reviewers). The strongest preserved disagreement is structural: Pike judges the underlying tagged-payload design correct and the issues purely documentary, while Hickey and Liskov view the seven near-identical preview classes, the overloaded meta, the missing supertype contract, and the kedro-core/kedro-viz module boundary as design problems the docs are papering over — implying that 'experimental' should signal more than stability, it should signal the taxonomy and contract themselves are likely to move. Torvalds additionally calls out PR hygiene (three patches in one, Vale ignore.txt drift, no tests anchoring the API claims) as merge-blocking, while Knuth and Dijkstra concur on the underlying spec gaps. Recommendation reflected across reviewers: tighten every code example to be runnable as written, state the preview_fn contract (purity, lifecycle, error semantics, return shape) before graduating from experimental, separate user-meta from render-config, and split the Vale config edits out of the docs PR.
